minutes.headline: Select Board held a site visit on Flat Hill Road drainage; no vote, engineer will review the 1990s plans next.
minutes.summary: The Select Board met on site at Flat Hill Road and Cortland Circle to see flooding and drainage problems firsthand. Residents described decades of water issues, and the town's consulting engineer explained that very high groundwater limits stormwater fixes along the road shoulders. The engineer will obtain and review the original development drainage plans and precipitation data before proposing a fix; nothing was voted.

Resident at 49 Cortland Circle describes flooding since 2005, landscaping drains and the septic system changing flow.
Residents at 268 describe water coming from behind their property and basement flooding.
Resident worried that piping water down to Flat Hill and Beaver Brook would worsen conditions on Page Street culverts and high water table.
Resident says sump pump runs almost constantly and water level has risen since 2004.
Resident with private pond concerned about town directing water to the farm and notification of abutters.

Resident concerned about water toward neighbors' houses and a bus stop icing in winter.

what_happened.line: The Select Board held a site visit on Flat Hill Road and Cortland Circle to see flooding and drainage problems firsthand; no vote was taken.
Residents described flooding that they said goes back to the 1990s development, including basement water, constantly running sump pumps and failed earlier fixes.
The town's consulting engineer said high groundwater limits stormwater fixes on the road shoulders, and that the cost would far outweigh the benefit.
The engineer will get electronic copies of the original development drainage plans and review them with precipitation data before recommending a fix.
No further survey is needed now; investigating the plans and groundwater comes next.

why_it_matters: Neighbors on Flat Hill Road and Cortland Circle have no fix yet, and any drainage work the town later proposes would be a public works cost that could come before voters as a budget item.

Residents elsewhere along the Beaver Brook and Page Street drainage path raised concern that moving water downstream could worsen conditions for them, so a fix may affect more than the streets visited.
